output.summary: KEP-2264 defines a release and CI process for the Kubernetes-CSI components maintained by sig-storage, with each component released separately and tested on Kubernetes before release. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale: The release process was manual, with some Travis CI help, and pre-release components were not automatically tested on a Kubernetes cluster. With CSI GA in Kubernetes 1.13, the project wanted a less work-intensive and more predictable approach. The design makes unit tests mandatory pre-submit for all components and Kubernetes testing mandatory for components deployed in a cluster.

alternatives.option: Automatically updating deployments by setting additional image tags (semantic versioning tags)
alternatives.why_not: Rejected in discussion because of the risks of automatically changing versions in a production cluster.

alternatives.option: Maintain the deployment in a separate repository with independent versioning
alternatives.why_not: Rejected because it is more work and because driver and deployment always need to be updated together.

alternatives.option: A combined Kubernetes-CSI release of all components
alternatives.why_not: Listed as a non-goal; each component is released separately and driver maintainers pick and test sidecar releases themselves.

evidence.quote: So far, the process for tagging and building components has been fairly manual, with some assistance by Travis CI.
With CSI support reaching GA in Kubernetes 1.13, it is time to define and follow a less work-intensive and more predictable approach.
a combined "Kubernetes-CSI release": each component gets released separately.
rejected that idea because of the risks associated with automatically changing versions in a production cluster.
The alternative would have been to maintain the deployment in a separate repository with its own independent versioning, but that has been rejected because it is more work
